note: GD.13 (from FD.43; DT.1e / DT.1f residuals): the Go server wire reader's three missed forms. (1) An encoder held in a local: `enc := json.NewEncoder(w); enc.Encode(o)` with w an http.ResponseWriter is the JSON response `json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(o)` is (implicit 200). (2) gin's explicit-binding forms `c.ShouldBindWith(&v, binding.JSON)` / `c.ShouldBindBodyWith(&v, binding.JSON)` are JSON binds when the binder is gin/binding's JSON through this file's import; another binder (`binding.Query`) binds no JSON body. (3) A handler that passes its context to a same-file helper (photoprism's `BindOAuthRequest(c *gin.Context, frm any)` shape, called as `bindRequest(c, &t)`): the helper's body is read once with its parameters mapped back to the caller's arguments, so the handler, not the helper, holds the json_bind of the caller's `t` and USES TokenRequest; the helper's own site binds an `any` parameter, which types nothing. The Go build types each cell's value to its STRUCT (DT.1f) and draws handler -USES-> STRUCT, EVIDENCE graph:go_wire rule json_response / json_bind.
